data.title: Glutamine alleviates bisphenol A-induced jejunal injury in piglets involving mitochondrial function restoration and AMPK-mTOR signaling regulation.
data.authors: Xie J; Liu Z; Liu W et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Glutamine supplementation alleviated bisphenol A-induced jejunal injury in piglets, restoring mitochondrial energy metabolism and barrier integrity alongside modulation of AMPK-mTOR signalling.
data.abstract_excerpt: Bisphenol A (BPA) disrupts intestinal homeostasis and promotes epithelial injury in piglets. Glutamine (Gln) is a vital energy substrate for intestinal epithelial cells. Piglet and porcine intestinal epithelial cell models were used. BPA exposure impaired intestinal morphology and barrier integrity, with reduced tight junction protein expression, decreased epithelial renewal capacity, altered JNK/MAPK signaling and disrupted mitochondrial structure and energy metabolism.

extracted_findings.effect: Improved tight junction expression, epithelial renewal and mitochondrial function under BPA stress
